issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 5.3, the proof asserts that there exists an index M independent of n such that the sets stabilize or become nested for all m >= M. This claim is false: in Lemma 5.1, the stabilization of the cover at resolution 2^{-n} requires the approximation error of \Phi_m to be bounded by the discretization step 2^{-n}. Because assumption (S2) provides no a priori uniform rate of convergence for \Phi_m, the index m required to achieve this tolerance must grow to infinity as n -> infinity; an index M independent of n would force \Phi_M to match the exact distance to the spectrum. Because stabilization fails uniformly in n, the subsequent interchange of the limit n_1 -> infinity with the maximum over k <= n_1 is invalid: the diagonal terms where k is close to n_1 evaluate covers at exponential resolution 2^{k+1} with only n_1 truncation steps, which have not converged.

failure_location.quote: \cref{lem:cover1}'s proof shows there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m}(A)\subset\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m+1}(A)$ for all $m\geq M$, independent of $n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the classification of the upper box-counting dimension under (S2) to \Pi_3^A (and that of the box-counting dimension on \widehat{\Omega} to \Delta_3^A), computing the quantity via three successive limits without collapsing the cover-approximation limit.
issues.overall_effect: The claims that the upper box-counting dimension lies in \Pi_2^A under (S2) and that the box-counting dimension on \widehat{\Omega} lies in \Pi_2^A under (S2) are unproven and false as constructed. The advertised reduction in the number of limits compared to Theorem 3.2 is invalid.
issues.title: False uniform stabilization and invalid limit interchange for upper box-counting dimension under (S2)
issues.why_classification: Any mathematically sound repair supported by the framework of the paper requires adding an extra limit to the algorithm tower (increasing the classification from \Pi_2^A to \Pi_3^A), which materially worsens the complexity guarantee and retracts the primary claim and advertised surprise of Theorem 5.3.
